card.title: Impulse
card.says: the **vector** change in momentum $\Delta\vec{p}$ caused by an average impulsive force $\vec{F}_{\text{av}}$ acting over contact time $\Delta t$. For the same $\Delta\vec{p}$, stretching out $\Delta t$ lowers the average force.
card.from: multiplying Newton's second law $\vec{F}_{\text{av}} = \dfrac{\Delta\vec{p}}{\Delta t}$ by $\Delta t$; when the force varies in time, impulse equals the area under the $F$–$t$ graph.
card.useWhen: a ball rebounds off a wall or racket, a car hits a barrier, or you need the average impulsive force during a brief impact—remember the minus sign when velocity reverses.
card.example: A $0.2\text{ kg}$ ball hits a wall at $u = +10\text{ m/s}$ and rebounds at $v = -8\text{ m/s}$ over $\Delta t = 0.04\text{ s}$: $I = 0.2(-8 - 10) = -3.6\text{ N}\cdot\text{s}$, so $F_{\text{av}} = \dfrac{-3.6}{0.04} = -90\text{ N}$.
card.analogy: Bending your knees when landing from a jump—or an airbag inflating in a crash—does not change your $\Delta p$, but it lengthens $\Delta t$ so the average force on your body stays much smaller.
